sections.title: Habit and identification
sections.text: Cumin is an upright, branched annual about 15–30 cm tall. Its leaves are finely divided into thread-like segments; small umbels bear the flowers and dry fruits. It is cultivated for its spice.

sections.title: Fruits used as spice
sections.text: The fruits, commonly called cumin seeds in cooking, are about 4–6 × 2 mm and harvested dry. The plate matches the fine foliage, umbels and elongated fruits. This is cumin, distinct from caraway, Carum carvi.
